title: plugbricks plugin manifest
description: Describes what a plugin is (image, port, dependencies), never how to run it. No Docker Compose or Kubernetes YAML belongs here.

name.description: Plugin identity. Used in network names: <plugin>-<service>.

tags.description: Free-form labels, for filtering in the admin (api, graphql, database, auth, ...). Sorted in the lock.

provides.description: Capabilities this plugin provides, keyed by capability name (e.g. database, queue).

requires.description: Capabilities this plugin needs, keyed by capability name. The resolver activates a missing provider.

extends.description: Entities owned by another plugin that this subgraph extends. The resolver activates the owner.

dependencies.description: Plugins this plugin needs to work, besides the capabilities it requires and the entities it extends: for example a web plugin that reads its data through the router needs the API plugin that serves it. The admin shows these links in its Dependencies tab. remove refuses a plugin that an installed plugin lists here, and disable refuses it while the declaring plugin is enabled (DEPENDENCY_IN_USE); add prints a warning when a listed plugin is not installed. An entry marked optional is none of that: it is only shown, and used for the roles it asks (D22). plugbricks does not install them or order startup by them (a capability in requires does).

wait.description: When the consumer may start: once the provider's ready command succeeds (healthy) or as soon as its container runs (started).

timeoutSeconds.description: How long the consumer waits for the provider before giving up. Docker Compose: the driver stops waiting and fails with WAIT_TIMEOUT. Kubernetes: the wait initContainer itself exits non-zero after timeoutSeconds, the pod ends in Init:Error then CrashLoopBackOff, and `plugbricks status` reports that state as WAIT_TIMEOUT.

optional.description: The brick runs without this capability: with no provider installed (or it is disabled) nothing is injected and nothing waits; with one, it is wired like any requirement. Resolved when the plan is built, so a provider added later wires it (D19).

image.description: Image reference. Pin a version; a floating tag such as :latest is rejected by the resolver.

extraPorts.description: Additional ports the service listens on. Kubernetes: extra ports of its Service, so that a provision task or an operator in the platform can reach them; Compose needs nothing (containers of the platform network reach any port). Never published on the host (D9). Use it for a management or metrics API, not for a second service.

name.description: Kubernetes Service port name: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, at most 15 characters. "main" is reserved for the primary port; names and port numbers must be unique within the service.

retention.description: What happens to the data when the plugin is removed: retain keeps the volume, delete removes it.

healthcheck.description: Readiness of this service. Docker Compose: healthcheck. Kubernetes: readinessProbe (never a livenessProbe), plus a startupProbe when startPeriodSeconds > 0. A service without healthcheck is reported as running with unknown health, never as healthy.

exec.description: Command run inside the container. Exec probes only: they translate to both runtimes.

timeoutSeconds.description: Limit for one attempt. Always set explicitly by the drivers, because Kubernetes defaults to 1s and Docker Compose to 30s.

startPeriodSeconds.description: Grace period after start during which failures do not count (Compose start_period, Kubernetes startupProbe).

env.description: Static variables. The only template allowed is ${secrets.<name>} (a secret generated by plugbricks, owned by this brick); never put a secret in clear here. A lone $ is literal.

service.description: Name of the service (in this manifest) that serves the capability.

ready.description: How a consumer checks, from outside the provider, that the capability accepts connections. Drivers run it before a consumer with wait=healthy starts (Kubernetes: an initContainer).

exec.description: Command, without a shell, that exits 0 when the capability is ready. Must target ${provider.host}; may use ${provider.port}.

image.description: Image to run the command in; it must contain /bin/sh, date and sleep (the wait loop). Default: the image of provides.<capability>.service. Same pinning rule as services[].image.

provision.description: One-shot task run once per consumer, before it starts. Must be idempotent (create if absent).

image.description: Image reference. Same pinning rule as services[].image.

command.description: Full argv, run without a shell; it replaces the image entrypoint. Templates: ${provider.host}, ${provider.port}, ${consumer.name}; never a secret (pass secrets through env).

scripts.description: Directory shipped with the plugin, relative to the manifest, mounted read-only at /provision in the task container.

inject.description: Variables added to the consumer's environment. Templates: ${consumer.name}, ${provider.host}, ${provider.port}, ${secrets.<name>}. A secret this brick's own services also use is the brick's; any other secret is generated per consumer.

schema.description: Path of the SDL file shipped with the plugin, relative to the manifest. Composition never uses introspection.

plugin.description: The name of the plugin this one needs.

description.description: Why it is needed, shown next to the link.

optional.description: The plugin works without the target (a page that shows more when the API is there): remove and disable do not refuse the target, add does not warn when it is missing, and the admin shows the link as optional. The operations it uses are still granted when the target is installed.

operations.description: What this plugin does to the target through its GraphQL API, when the target declares an "authorization" block (D22): the platform gives this plugin's service account the target's role for each operation class listed here, and only those. Reading is the default; write "mutations" to be allowed to change data. Nothing is granted for a class the target left open, and nothing at all without a provider of "oidc".

authorization.description: Who may call this plugin's GraphQL API, by operation class (D22). Each value is the name of a client role of this plugin's own OIDC client (the client the oidc provider creates for it, named like the plugin): a token that does not carry it is refused with the GraphQL code FORBIDDEN, after it was found valid. A class left out stays at D20: any valid token. Applies only when an enabled brick provides "oidc"; without one nothing is enforced. Needs a "subgraph" and "requires.oidc" (optional is fine).

queries.description: The role needed to run a query on this API.

mutations.description: The role needed to run a mutation on this API.

web.description: The service that serves web pages on its port (D17). The platform publishes it on its own loopback port (webPort in platform.json) and, when a router exists, gives that service GRAPHQL_URL (the router inside the platform) and PUBLIC_GRAPHQL_URL (the router as a browser on this machine reaches it).

path.description: Entry page, shown by the admin.

oidc.description: On a web brick that provides oidc: what the router needs to check its tokens (D19). The issuer is the brick's web origin plus issuerPath; the keys are fetched inside the platform at the provider's service plus jwksPath; only tokens for this audience are accepted.
